jobs.title: Sr Robotics Engineer, PWT
jobs.description:
About Lucid 

 At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.   

 We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility. 

Position Overview 

The Sr Robotics Engineer, Powertrain owns robotics standards, offline programming, reliability, and safety validation for AMP-2 Powertrain — covering both Drive Unit and HV Battery robotic populations. Joining a greenfield facility, this engineer sets FANUC, ABB, and KUKA standards from first commissioning through volume ramp-up. The role is accountable for robot uptime, cycle time, and safety compliance for the entire Powertrain robot fleet. The role operates through disciplined change control, objective launch evidence, cross-functional problem solving, and structured transfer of technical ownership to the Saudi workforce.

Key Responsibilities 

1.              Robotics Standards & Architecture

 2.              Define and enforce robotics standards across FANUC, ABB, and KUKA populations

 3.              Establish naming, positional, program, and safety-configuration standards

 4.              Own robot BOM standards including controllers, teach pendants, safety modules, and EOAT interfaces

 Offline Programming & Cell Design 

 1.              Own offline programming environments (FANUC RoboGuide, ABB RobotStudio, etc)

 2.              Perform reachability, collision, and cycle-time simulation for new cells and cell modifications

 3.              Support cell layout, safety zoning, and human–robot collaboration design

 Robot Reliability & Uptime 

 1.              Own robot uptime KPIs across the Powertrain fleet; drive downtime reduction through structured analysis

 2.              Establish robot PM strategy including grease, encoder, battery, and cable-track maintenance

 3.              Lead RCA for robot-related breakdowns and cell downtime

 Cycle Time Optimization 

 4.               Own robot cycle time optimization to support takt achievement

 5.               Deploy structured cycle-time reduction using motion tuning, path smoothing, and program optimization

 Robot Safety Validation 

 1.              Own robot safety validation

 2.              Coordinate with EHS and Automation on safety-PLC integration, light curtains, and interlocks

 3.              Ensure safety validation records are maintained and audit-ready

 HV Safety & Compliance 

 1.              Enforce HV LOTO, HVIL continuity, and mandatory HV PPE for all work on or near EV Powertrain equipment

 2.              Comply with SASO, Saudi MOL, IEC 60204, and functional safety standards (ISO 13849 / IEC 62061)

 3.              Support HV emergency response including thermal runaway isolation and battery-related incident procedures

 4.              Achieve and maintain HV safety competency appropriate to scope of work

 Launch Governance & Ramp-Up 

 1.              Support AMP-2 Safe Launch activities, run-at-rate events, and capacity verification within scope

 2.              Contribute to Launch Readiness Reviews, Layered Process Audits, and Process Confirmation routines

 3.              Participate in QRQC / RCCA escalations during launch and ramp-up phases

 Safety & Reliability Governance 

 1.              Define robot programming, naming, frame, payload, backup, mastering, spare, preventive-maintenance and controlled-change standards.

 2.              Own offline simulation, reachability, collision, safety zones, cycle optimization and digital validation for new cells and modifications.

 3.              Safe-speed/space functions, safety PLC interfaces and audit-ready validation records.

 4.              Establish fleet KPI, bad-actor analysis, obsolescence roadmap, recovery playbooks and engineer/technician qualification standards.

 Launch Governance, Change Control & Operational Readiness 

 1.              Support FAT/SAT, commissioning, equipment acceptance, Safe Launch, run-at-rate and capacity verification with objective evidence and disciplined punch-list closure.

 2.              Control production, process, software and test changes through documented risk assessment, approvals, validation, revision history and rollback or containment planning.

 3.              Participate in readiness reviews, Layered Process Audits, Process Confirmation and QRQC/RCCA; close assigned actions with verified effectiveness.

 Safety, Quality, Data Integrity & Compliance 

 1.              Apply role-specific HV LOTO/HVIL, machine safety, stored-energy isolation, electrical safe-work and PPE requirements; never bypass safety devices or product protections.

 2.              Protect product genealogy, calibrated-tool status, test/measurement integrity, document control and audit-ready objective evidence.

 3.              Comply with applicable AMP-2, SASO, Saudi labor/EHS, IATF 16949, IEC 60204 and functional-safety requirements within assigned scope.

 Saudization, Capability Transfer & Collaboration 

 1.              Build Saudi national capability through structured OJT, ILU/skills matrices, practical assessment, certification, cross-training and documented knowledge transfer.

 2.              Create technical standards, troubleshooting guides and training material;

 3.               Collaborate across Production, Quality, Maintenance, Automation/Robotics, Manufacturing Engineering, EHS, IT/OT, MES, Supply Chain, Product Engineering and suppliers.

Skills 

1.              Deep robotics expertise (FANUC, ABB, etc)

 2.              Strong offline programming skills (RoboGuide, RobotStudio, etc)

 3.              Robot safety validation fluency

 4.              Structured troubleshooting and reliability mindset

 5.              Passion for developing people on robotics talent

 6.              Technical standards, structured problem solving, risk-based decision making and controlled documentation

 7.              Data literacy: KPI definition, trend analysis, evidence-based validation and clear executive/shop-floor communication

 8.              Cross-functional influence, supplier coordination and disciplined ownership in a greenfield launch environment

 9.              Coaching, competency assessment and knowledge transfer in a multicultural English/Arabic workplace

Minimum Qualifications 

1.              Bachelor's degree in Mechatronics, Electrical, or Robotics Engineering

 2.              5 – 8  years in industrial robotics; multi-brand experience required especially Fanuc

 3.              Demonstrated robot commissioning, offline programming, and safety validation experience

 4.              Strong track record of robot uptime and cycle time optimization

 5.              Fluent in English; Arabic strongly preferred

 6.              Preferred: EV or automotive greenfield launch; and collaborative-robot experience

 7.              Demonstrated experience with commissioning, FAT/SAT, launch, production readiness or high-volume manufacturing ramp within the role discipline

 1.              Working knowledge of IATF 16949, APQP/change control, machine/HV safety and traceability requirements applicable to the role

 2.              Preferred: recognized discipline certification, Lean/Six Sigma, greenfield EV/automotive launch and KSA workforce-development experience

Compensation & Benefits:   Lucid offers a comprehensive and competitive  benefits package  including medical, dental, and vision insurance; life and disability coverage; paid time off; paid holidays, paid sick leave; and a 401(k) retirement plan. Hourly/non-exempt employees accrue up to 120 hours paid time off, and salaried/exempt employee accrue up to 160 hours paid time off.  Eligible employees may also participate in Lucid’s equity program and/or a discretionary annual cash incentive program. Senior Staff Software Engineer, Motion Planning and Controls, Autonomous Driving 

 Leading the future in luxury electric and mobility At Lucid, we set out to introduce the most captivating, luxury electric vehicles that elevate the human experience and transcend the perceived limitations of space, performance, and intelligence. Vehicles that are intuitive, liberating, and designed for the future of mobility. We plan to lead in this new era of luxury electric by returning to the fundamentals of great design – where every decision we make is in service of the individual and environment. Because when you are no longer bound by convention, you are free to define your own experience. Come work alongside some of the most accomplished minds in the industry. We’re providing a community for innovators who want to make an immediate and significant impact. If you are driven to create a better, more sustainable future, then this is the right place for you.

 Role Overview 

 We are seeking a Senior Staff Software Engineer to support the auto-parking and low-speed autonomy stack. This role focuses on trajectory optimization, path smoothing, and local planning, with direct impact on parking features such as Auto Park, Summon, and Park-to-Park. The ideal candidate will combine strong algorithmic foundations with production-grade software execution, driving both system performance and scalability. This role is based in Newark, CA. and requires employees to be onsite five days a week.

 Key Responsibilities: 

Motion Planning & Trajectory Optimization
 
 Develop and enhance trajectory optimization algorithms (e.g., iLQR / MPC-based approaches) for low-speed scenarios

 Design and implement constraint-aware optimization, including

 Improve local planners to generate control-friendly trajectories

System Architecture & Performance Optimization
 
 Refactor and scale planning stack architecture for maintainability and extensibility

 Optimize CPU usage and explore parallel/GPU acceleration opportunities

 Improve system-level behaviors such as:
 
 Stability under dynamic constraints

 Scalability across scenarios and vehicle platforms

Debugging, Validation, and Production Integration
 
 Investigate and resolve real-world issues such as: Curvature discontinuities, velocity/trajectory mismatches, and edge-case steering behavior

 Validate solutions using:
 
 Simulation and vehicle logs

 Multi-scenario testing and benchmarking

Research, Prototyping, and Innovation
 
 Evaluate and prototype new approaches (e.g., learned models, barrier functions, ML-based planning)

 Benchmark and compare planning algorithms for production viability

 Contribute to next-gen planning initiatives, including ML-driven planning

Cross-Team Collaboration & Knowledge Transfer
 
 Drive technical discussions and share algorithm insights across teams

 Maintain high-quality documentation and support knowledge transfer

 Track work via Jira with clear metrics and reproducible results

Required Qualifications: 

M.S. or Ph.D. in Robotics, Control, Electrical Engineering, or related field

 10+ years of software development experience in autonomous driving, ADAS, or robotics, with a focus on large-scale data and real-time systems

 Strong programming skills in C/C++ with solid understanding of software engineering design principles and best practices

 Proven track record of delivering ADAS/AD features through the full production lifecycle: requirements analysis, architecture/design, implementation, unit testing, feature tuning, SIL/HIL validation, and in-vehicle deployment

 Hands-on experience with software integration on embedded platforms (e.g., NVIDIA Xavier/Orin, Infineon Aurix)

 Demonstrated ability to build reliable production-grade systems, including large-scale architectures, evaluation pipelines, and performance-optimized models

 Leadership experience

Preferred Qualifications: 

ML-based planning approaches

 GPU or parallel computing for planning

 Track record of production deployment in real vehicles

 Lucid Motor’s Polymer Technology Team is an expert group sharing material, process and tooling insight where needed across the organization. The team drives all polymer-related aspects throughout the entire product development process and supports the organization beyond that by covering aspects of material vetting/selection/approval, engineering design optimization, design for manufacturing (DFM), process simulation, tool concept/design, process optimization, material characterization and failure analysis among other responsibilities.    

 The Sr. Plastics Engineer – Tooling and Process role strengthens the Tooling and Process Group by working on new developments, supporting DFM optimization, performing and analyzing process simulations, evaluating tool concepts/designs as well as through on-site support for process optimization and troubleshooting.    

   The Role:   

Be a significant contributor to a world-class vehicle engineering team by supporting with plastics tool expertise and owning polymer-related aspects from part design for manufacturing (DFM) phase to product launch   

 Consultation with design engineers and suppliers throughout product development process, advising on process and tooling feasibility, DFM, efficiency and cost. Role ensures capability, robustness and cost-effectiveness of tool with sign-off.   

 Evaluation of flow studies and mold designs before tool approval and kick-off   

 Ensuring plastic tooling is compliant with Lucid Tool Standards   

 On-site assessment of tool quality/condition, and driving injection molding process optimization through direct/specific improvement suggestions   

 Methodical approach to documentation   

 Support of internal non-engineering teams and representation of Lucid material team in communication with suppliers (incl. on-site visits)   

Qualifications:   

B.S.in polymer engineering or related field, or equivalent experience   

 5+ years’ experience, evaluating DFM and injection molding tool designs    

 Excellent knowledge of injection tooling, including technologies such as in-mold decoration/labeling, foaming, water/gas assist, overmolding, back-injection, vario-thermal processes   

 Experience with DFM process for automotive A-surface parts   

 Experience with flow simulation software (Autodesk MoldFlow)   

 Proven hands-on experience with plastic injection molding process, including process optimization   

 Exemplary verbal and written communication skills   

 Able to travel domestically and internationally up to 25% if needed   

Advantageous:   

Worked in automotive development environment, ideally through complete product development process   

 Hands-on experience with creation of MoldFlow studies, first tool trials, and tool approvals   

 Experience with tool should costing to understand tool cost impact of part design choices   

 Experience with other plastic manufacturing processes and their tooling (e.g. blow molding, thermal forming, vacuum forming, compression molding, slush molding)

 The  Sr. Production Control Support   supports inventory control, and kitting activities for engineering and prototype build operations. Working under the guidance of  Production Control  Specialists, Lab Managers, and Technical Project Managers . T his role helps ensure materials are available to support build schedules and engineering activities. The position  is responsible for   maintaining   inventory  accuracy, tracking parts, supporting procurement follow-up activities, and  assisting  with  build  readiness efforts. This is a hands-on role well suited for individuals looking to build experience in material management within a fast-paced prototype and R&D environment.   

Role: 

 Material Planning & Readiness  Support   

Support the review of engineering BOMs and build plans provided by Lab Managers and Technical Project Managers.   

 Assist in validating material availability and procurement status for upcoming builds.   

 Monitor material readiness and escalate potential shortages to senior team members.   

 Support build preparation activities by tracking required parts and materials.   

BOM Support & Configuration Management   

Assist with BOM validation and part-number verification.   

 Support review of engineering changes, alternate parts, and material updates.   

 Help maintain accurate records of BOM revisions and build configurations.   

Procurement Coordination   

Coordinate with GSMs, Buyers, and Logistics teams to monitor material deliveries.   

 Follow up on open purchase orders and shipment status.   

 Escalate delayed or at-risk materials to Material Specialists and stakeholders.   

 Support material requests for prototype and low-volume builds.   

Inventory & Material Tracking   

Monitor inventory levels and incoming shipments to support build schedules.   

 Track material movement between warehouses, labs, and staging areas.   

 Investigate inventory discrepancies and assist with corrective actions.   

 Maintain inventory accuracy through cycle counts and transaction audits.   

Kitting & Line Support   

Support kitting activities based on build schedules and technician requirements.   

 Create and process Pick Orders in SAP.   

 Prepare and maintain kitting lists, pull sheets, and material labels.   

 Respond to material requests from technicians and engineering teams.   

 Ensure kits are accurately staged and available when needed.   

Reporting & Communication   

Update material tracking tools, dashboards, and status reports.   

 Communicate part shortages, late deliveries, and inventory issues to the team.   

 Participate in prototype readiness meetings and provide material status updates.   

 Maintain accurate documentation of material transactions and build support activities.   

Change Control Support   

Assist with Engineering Change Orders (ECOs) that impact material requirements.   

 Support the tracking of material substitutions and part revisions.   

 Maintain documentation to support traceability requirements.   

Qualifications: 

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Business, or a related field preferred.   

 Equivalent experience in material control, inventory management, warehouse operations, or manufacturing support may be considered.   

 3-5 years of experience in inventory control, warehouse operations, or production support.   

 Experience in manufacturing, prototype, engineering, or supply chain environments is preferred.   

 Basic knowledge of ERP systems such as SAP is preferred.   

 Proficiency in Microsoft Excel; experience with Smartsheet is a plus.   

 Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

jobs.title: Sr. Test Engineer
jobs.description:
About Lucid 

 At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.   

 We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility. 

 The Sr. Manufacturing Test Engineer will play a lead role in advancing Lucid’s goal of being a highly automated manufacturing company. They will work closely with external equipment suppliers and internal teams including Engineering, Quality, Production, and Maintenance to design, program, test, and commission complex automated test systems.

You Will:

Review and approve Test Specifications and change requests from the design engineering team. Act as the manufacturing engineering representative to analyze and provide feedback on test sequence and parameters, cycle time, process flow for various test failure modes, etc.

 Design test system hardware to implement test requirements. This includes system layout, component selection, cabinet/rack design, selection and sizing of connectors and cables, with consideration for heat loads, electrical noise, and ease of access for troubleshooting

 Develop modular test applications with intuitive and informative GUIs. Utilize databases to store test parameters and log test data. Implement user access control to allow modifying test sequences and parameters from the GUI

 Provide inputs to test station design including DUT handling and connection methods. Specify test application interface with station control system. Collaborate with controls engineers to develop overall station sequence, and responses to different failure modes

 Manage test equipment sourcing, build, and validation by internal and external teams. For externally sourced equipment, create RFQs, select suppliers and track their progress to ensure timely delivery

 Develop commissioning and validation plans for test equipment including Gauge Reliability and Repeatability tests, red-rabbits, and injection/simulation of various failure modes

 Launch test systems on manufacturing lines. Collaborate with cross functional teams to monitor functionality and performance. Train maintenance and operations teams on error recovery and troubleshooting techniques. Collaborate with factory data visualization teams on creating dashboards

You Bring: 

Bachelor’s, Masters, or PhD Degree in Engineering required (Preferred Electrical or Electronics Engineering)

 5+ years of experience developing automated test equipment for manufacturing

 Experience in launching automated test systems on high volume manufacturing lines

 Experience in testing electric vehicle powertrain components is a plus

 Detailed knowledge of electrical & electronics circuits and components, cables and connectors

 Ability to design electrical schematics using AutoCAD or Eplan

 Knowledge and experience in developing test system hardware using National Instruments platforms such as PXI, cDAQ, cRIO

 Expertise in developing test application software using one or more software tools such as NI LabVIEW, NI TestStand, NI Veristand, Python, Arduino IDE, MATLAB

 Knowledge of communication protocols like Automotive Ethernet, CAN, LIN etc.,

 Ability to use electrical test equipment such as power supplies, multimeters, oscilloscopes, power analyzers, etc. for validation and troubleshooting

 Knowledge of Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC) and industrial communication protocols such as Ethernet/IP, OPC-UA etc. is a plus

 Strong organization skills – tracking schedule and open items, creating meeting agendas and minutes

In this role you will own validation strategy and execution for assigned power electronics programs, author and drive DVP&Rs from requirements through closure, and architect system-level test setups that scale across programs. You will work autonomously, set technical direction for test methodology, and mentor junior engineers and technicians.

Responsibilities

Own and drive verification and validation strategy for power electronics products (on-board chargers, DC-DC converters, inverters, and related high voltage assemblies) from concept through production release.

 Author, own, and drive DVP&Rs: derive test cases from system and component requirements, define acceptance criteria and sample sizes, negotiate scope and schedule with design and program teams, and drive plans to closure with documented evidence.

 Architect system-level test setups and validation architectures, including HV/LV interfaces, load and mission profiles, thermal and environmental conditioning, fault-insertion, and end-to-end data acquisition strategy.

 Review electrical and mechanical schematics and define test cell layouts and requirements for instrumentation, low voltage, and high voltage circuitry; specify equipment and drive lab capability build-out.

 Define and oversee the design of test benches including jigs and fixtures, instrumentation, harnessing, and DAQ systems; establish measurement accuracy, uncertainty, and correlation requirements.

 Lead root-cause analysis of complex system-level failures, drive corrective action with design and supplier teams, and independently drive R&D and design-improvement activities.

 Establish test methods, procedures, and best practices; standardize automation, data pipelines, and reporting across the team.

 Serve as the validation technical interface to design, systems, reliability, quality, manufacturing, and supplier teams; represent test results in design reviews and program gate reviews.

 Mentor and provide technical direction to junior engineers and technicians; review test plans, setups, data, and reports for technical rigor.

 Own HV lab safety standards, equipment calibration strategy, and documentation quality for the validation area.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or higher in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Power Electronics, or a related field.

 5+ years of experience in power electronics development, test, and validation.

 Deep understanding of power electronics fundamentals (switching topologies, magnetics, gate drive,

 Restraints team has responsibility over the airbags, seatbelts, and steering wheels at Lucid Motors, taking the inputs from interfacing teams and the technical product description, and managing the products from concept through the production life such that they meet all requirements. What is unique about Lucid Restraints, and Lucid more broadly, is the opportunity and expectation for each individual to gain autonomy and take ownership of their product area, while making decisions in collaboration with ( and in support of ) the broader team’s expertise. 

   About the Role   

 We are currently seeking a  Sr. Engineer, Seatbelts , reporting to the Manager of Steering Wheel Unit and Seatbelts. This position requires an excellent understanding of mechanical engineering fundamentals with enough experience with Seat Belt system development to be responsible for seatbelt projects with autonomy. Candidates will be expected to demonstrate excellence in their respective fields, to possess the ability to learn quickly and to strive for perfection within a fast-paced environment. The candidate with the target experience and ability would have the opportunity to define the strategy and architecture of the seatbelt system, and influence our design processes and methods used for assessment. The role would start with sustaining existing projects and developing their new variants and derivatives, but is expected to have increasing duties on new development over time. 

 What You Own    

Develop and sustain seat belts systems, across the whole product lifetime: from system specification development, sourcing, packaging, drawing release, design validation to ramp up, manufacturing support to post SOP maintenance.  

 Achieve product technical excellence as well as economical, timing and quality targets. 

 Collaborate with the design studio, ergonomic, seating, BIW and interior engineering teams to develop the optimum restraint system packages for occupant protection performance and interior styling. 

 Provide guidance and requirements to internal teams on required reaction forces or displacements, keep out zones, and lead conceptual design of required guides, brackets, etc.  

 Manage Tier 1 suppliers for both engineering development and program timing. Function as the main point of contact for all supplier interfaces. 

 Support restraint system integration work: 1) Seatbelt integration into seat, BIW and other surrounding vehicle environments, accounting for seat kinematics and related interactions during crash events. 2)Provide expertise on restraint system design to help achieve regulatory and consumer safety targets for our new vehicles. Work closely with CAE and Crash Test teams to provide design inputs and utilize CAE and test results to optimize the component design. 

  Support crash tests and vehicle homologation. Make sure parts are supplied with correct pedigrees for all crash test vehicles and other vehicle level validation and homologation needs. 

What You Bring   

 Minimum Qualifications   

Deep understanding of Mechanical Engineering fundamentals: mechanics of materials, materials properties, dynamics and biomechanics related to occupant safety, failure mechanics 

 Strong analytical and problem-solving skill to apply the engineering knowledge to solving practical problems 

 Enough CAD skills to package the component models into the vehicle environment, and check and define interfaces with the rest of the vehicle. The ideal candidate should possess enough CAD skills to design brackets, fixtures, or offer proposals for modifications of the seatbelt and interfacing hardware. 

 Strong ethics and diligence 

 Bachelor’s degree or above in Mechanical Engineering or other related fields 

 Generally, requires 5+years of related experience

Preferred Qualifications   

Design and engineering of seat belts systems at an automotive OEM or Tier 1 supplier having direct responsibility of Product Development and System Integration. 

 Knowledge of seatbelt regulatory and consumer test requirements and strategies. 

 Knowledge of the latest technological advancement in the field of Seat Belts 

 Knowledge about metal parts forming, plastic injection molding , and associated design rules 

 Experience using GD&T and tolerance stack analysis (ASME or ISO) 

 Experience using APQP processes (DVP&R, 8D, DFMEA, DRBFM) 

 Strong oral and written communication skills to be able to articulate highly technical issues for general audiences not in the crash safety field, such as top management, design studio, purchasing team, etc. 

 Strong ownership mindset to work independently and fulfil the tasks in a timely manner.  

 Excellent soft skills to manage suppliers, push the envelope to develop optimal technical solutions, ensure timely delivery of all components 

 Knowledge of CAE analysis (e.g., LS-Dyna) and restraint system integration and optimization 

 6 sigma Green or Black Belt

 Develop and execute commissioning and validation plans for inverter test systems, including GR&R, red‑rabbit units, fault injection, and simulation of electrical, thermal, and communication failures.

 Launch inverter test systems into production and provide on‑floor support during ramp, including limit tuning, yield improvement, and false‑fail reduction.

 Train maintenance and operations teams on inverter test station operation, error recovery, and safe troubleshooting of high‑voltage power electronics.

 Partner with factory data and analytics teams to enable inverter test data visualization, yield tracking, efficiency trends, and long‑term quality monitoring.

 5~8 years of experience developing and launching automated test equipment in high‑volume manufacturing environments.

 Direct experience testing EV traction inverters or high‑power power electronics in a manufacturing or production setting.

 Strong understanding of inverter architectures, power stages, gate drivers, DC‑link capacitors, current sensing, and thermal management.

 Hands‑on experience with inverter EOL and in‑process testing such as functional power testing, PWM validation, phase current measurement, switching performance, efficiency testing, isolation resistance, and hipot testing.

 Detailed knowledge of high‑voltage and high‑current electrical components, connectors, cables, shielding, and grounding best practices.

 Ability to design electrical schematics using AutoCAD, EPLAN, or equivalent tools.

 Experience developing test hardware using National Instruments platforms such as PXI, cDAQ, or cRIO.

 Working knowledge of automotive communication protocols including CAN, CAN‑FD, LIN, and Automotive Ethernet, including inverter diagnostics and calibration interfaces.

 Experience in phased-array antenna development & optimization including AoA estimation & beamforming. 

 Experience in passive-entry localization technologies such as UWB & Bluetooth LE Channel Sounding.

 Expertise in RF coexistence and de-sense mitigation through simulation, analysis, and troubleshooting.

 Expertise in predicting & optimizing vehicle-level wireless performance through comprehensive end to end RF link budget analysis.

 Familiar with regulatory & carrier certification requirements for FCC, CE, PTCRB, AT&T, T-Mobile etc.

 Knowledge of wireless chipset selection, characterization & board level integration design & optimization.

 This position requires a seasoned professional with deep  expertise  in  higher levels of driving automation , a strong understanding of the transition from L2+ assisted driving to conditionally and highly automated (L3/L4) driving, and a proven  track record  of bringing innovative ADAS/AD software features into production. Our ideal candidate  exhibits  a can-do attitude, approaches their work with vigor and determination, and thrives in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.   

ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES   

Conceptualize, prototype, and launch cutting-edge L2++/L3/L4 driving features, including but not limited to:    

Hands-off highway driving with driver monitoring system (DMS) supervision   

Automated lane changes and highway merge/exit maneuvers   

Urban automated driving (intersections, traffic signals, roundabouts)   

Conditional automation (L3) with fallback-ready transition of control (ToC) strategies   

Geo-fenced L4 highway pilot with minimal driver intervention   

Advanced longitudinal and lateral control (steering, braking, acceleration) on ODD-defined roads   

Own the end-to-end feature lifecycle from concept through production launch ensuring timely delivery of fully validated high-quality customer features    

Create and manage feature roadmaps for multiple vehicle program lines, securing buy-in from stakeholders including marketing, homologation, safety, and executive leadership    

Serve as the voice of the customer, representing L2++/L3/L4 features in all internal and external communications    

Develop comprehensive feature definitions, including use cases, operational design domains (ODD), functional requirements, and target performance KPIs    

Collaborate closely with the Functional Safety team to facilitate HARA, Safety Goal development, and SOTIF (Safety of the Intended Functionality) analysis specific to higher automation levels    

Drive feature specifications using creative ideas and lead usability studies with UX/UI design teams, focusing on seamless handoff experiences between automated and manual driving    

Partner with Tier 1 suppliers and internal teams (perception, planning, controls, mapping) to implement innovative L2++/L3/L4 solutions    

Lead competitive benchmarking to stay current with industry trends, emerging regulations, and competitor L3/L4 offerings    

Work cross-functionally with systems engineering, software, validation, and homologation teams to ensure seamless and robust feature development and delivery    

Support V&V strategy development for higher automation features, including scenario-based testing, simulation, and real-world validation approaches  

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:   

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Electrical Engineering, Automotive Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field    

8+ years of hands-on experience in ADAS/AD feature development, with a focus on L2+ and above driving automation features   

Proven track record of bringing ADAS/AD driving features into production (e.g., highway assist, traffic jam pilot, automated lane change, hands-off driving)    

Strong expertise in use case development, ODD definition, and requirements engineering for L2++/L3/L4 features    

Solid understanding of SAE J3016 automation levels and the functional/architectural differences between L2+, L3, and L4 systems    

Experience with automotive supplier interaction, specification development, project/release management, and change management    

Strong understanding of regulations and standards relevant to higher automation:    

Regulations: FMVSS, GSR, ECE R79, ECE R157, DCAS-R171   

Standards: ISO 26262, ISO/PAS 21448 (SOTIF), ASPICE, ISO 34502/34503   

Proficiency with  requirements management tools  (JAMA, DOORS, etc.)    

Proficiency with  agile development tools  such as JIRA    

Excellent communication skills and ability to present complex automation concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences   

Preferred Qualifications:   

Master’s degree in systems engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field   

Previous experience as a Feature Owner or Product Owner for L2+/L3/L4 driving functions at an OEM or Tier 1 supplier   

Experience with driver monitoring systems (DMS) and their integration with hands-off/eyes-off driving modes   

Familiarity with scenario-based testing frameworks, simulation tools (e.g., dSPACE, CarMaker, CARLA), and SiL/HiL validation for AD features   

Knowledge of perception sensor suites (camera, radar, LiDAR, ultrasonics) and sensor fusion architectures relevant to L3/L4   

Understanding of motion planning, path planning, and decision-making algorithms at a conceptual level   

Experience with Euro NCAP testing and scoring methodologies, particularly for assisted driving grading schemes   

Knowledge of in-vehicle communication protocols (CAN, LIN, Automotive Ethernet)   

Experience with feature-level project management and ADAS software development processes   

Familiarity with OTA (Over-the-Air) update strategies for iterative feature deployment

CFD experience and familiarity with tools such as GT-Suite and TAI Therm.

 At least 2 years of experience with thermal comfort modeling/testing.

 Experience and knowledge of electric vehicles, including batteries, drive units, motor control, power electronics, thermal systems, and vehicle communication networks.

 A proven track record of technical excellence in a field relevant to this role.

 Based in Newark, California, with hands-on vehicle instrumentation and thermal comfort testing. Confirm the onsite schedule, travel, and any applicable physical requirements with the hiring manager.

 EMC/EMI testing knowledge.

The Role 

 We are looking for a software engineer to help build the data platform that supports  autonomous  vehicle development. You will collaborate closely with internal customers to deliver reliable, scalable, and efficient solutions that enable data-driven development of  autonomous  vehicle technologies.

Responsibilities 

Design, build, and maintain backend services and data pipelines for ingesting, processing, storing, and serving sensor datasets.

 Develop reliable and scalable systems using Python and AWS cloud services.

 Build APIs, data services, and tooling that enable efficient access to  autonomous  vehicle data.

 Improve platform reliability, observability, performance, and operational efficiency.

 Own production services and participate in troubleshooting, incident response, and root cause analysis.

 Collaborate cross-functionally with internal and external teams to understand requirements and deliver scalable solutions.

 Optimize  storage, compute, and data movement costs while maintaining high performance and availability.

 Contribute to architecture discussions, code reviews, and engineering best practices.

 Support CI/CD, infrastructure automation, and operational excellence across the platform.

Required Qualifications 

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

 3+ years of professional software engineering experience

 Strong software development experience in Python.

 Experience building and operating backend services, distributed systems, or large-scale data platforms.

Professional experience with AWS and deploying applications to Kubernetes clusters.

Experience with Airflow or other workflow orchestrators

Experience designing data pipelines, ETL systems, or data processing frameworks.

 Experience developing containerized applications, backend microservices, and event-driven systems or data pipelines.

 Past experience in the  Autonomous Driving or automotive  industry, specifically backend and cloud development.

Strong ownership mindset with the ability to drive projects from design through production operations.

 Experience building distributed systems or data platforms that process large-scale datasets in cloud environments.

Position Overview 

The Senior Engineer, Chassis Systems is responsible for ensuring chassis manufacturing quality through successful execution and continuous improvement of chassis system assembly, wheel alignment processes, torque-controlled joint assembly, wheel and tire installation, and end-of-line vehicle validation.

 The role serves as the primary technical interface between Vehicle Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Controls, Supplier Quality, Service Engineering, and Plant Operations to ensure all vehicles meet alignment, handling, safety, and customer satisfaction targets before shipment.

Responsible for sustaining engineering after initial product launch. This includes design and release of new parts as required such as to improve quality or the assembly process. Working with core engineering to ensure parts meet all design and validation requirements.     

Key Responsibilities 

Chassis System Assembly Ownership 

 - Serve as plant technical lead for chassis assembly operations including front and rear suspension modules, steering system installation, brake system installation, wheels and tires, subframe marriage processes, spring/damper/air suspension assembly, and steering gear/tie rod/knuckle assembly.

 - Ensure chassis assembly processes achieve safety, quality, throughput, and cost objectives.

 - Partner with Manufacturing Engineering to develop and optimize assembly sequences, tooling, ergonomics, and workstation layouts.

 - Support assembly process validation during prototype, pilot, and production builds.

 - Investigate and resolve assembly-related concerns including part fit-up issues, excessive installation force, dimensional variation, and fastener accessibility concerns.

 - Lead root cause analysis of manufacturing defects resulting from chassis assembly processes.

 Joint Tightening & Fastening Integrity 

 - Own production issue resolution related to chassis joint integrity and torque-controlled assembly processes.

 - Support tightening strategy, torque traceability, tool capability, process controls, and fastener accessibility improvements.

 - Partner with Manufacturing Engineering, Controls, and Quality to improve joint quality and reduce rework.

 Wheel Alignment & Vehicle Geometry 

 - Serve as plant technical lead for front and rear wheel alignment, camber, caster, toe, thrust angle, ride height settings, ClearVision performance, pull/drift performance, and steering wheel centering.

 - Support optimization of automated wheel alignment stations, alignment equipment, and plant tooling.

 - Establish robust alignment specifications and process controls.

 - Investigate alignment-related customer concerns and warranty claims.

 - Drive reduction in wheel alignment variability across production.

 - Support development and improvement of alignment stations, ride-height measurement systems, steering angle verification, pull/drift audits, and ClearVision audits.

 - Lead troubleshooting of end-of-line equipment and process failures.

 Wheels, Tires & End-of-Line Quality Validation 

 - Serve as technical owner for wheel assemblies, tire fitment, wheel balancing, tire pressure process controls, and assembly variation management.

 - Support end-of-line vehicle validation activities for chassis-related performance, geometry, handling, and customer satisfaction targets.

 - Support production launch readiness, issue tracking, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.

Sustaining Engineering 

 - Responsible for the design and development of automative chassis components and assemblies to deliver the highest level of performance in NVH, Durability, and Manufacturability while optimizing cost.  

 - Work closely with other stake owners and attribute owners across the company such as Core engineering.  Vehicle Safety, Vehicle Dynamics, NVH, Durability, Manufacturing, Design Studio, etc.

 - Cross functionally works with Manufacturing, Design and Product Development as well as with Purchasing, Supplier Quality, and Suppliers on items such as tool buy-offs and secondary component changes.

Skills 

- Deep understanding of wheel alignment theory, tire behavior, steering systems, chassis fastening systems, vehicle handling fundamentals, and chassis system assembly processes.

 - Working knowledge of wheel alignment, chassis integration, manufacturing engineering, quality engineering, and vehicle launch support.

 - Hands-on knowledge of GD&T, root cause analysis, DFMEA, PFMEA, statistical process control, and production issue resolution.

 - Experience or familiarity with Duerr alignment equipment, Atlas Copco tightening systems, torque traceability systems, and Minitab.

 - Knowledge of vehicle pull, drift, ClearVision, and steering performance assessments.

 - Strong technical ownership, data-driven decision making, continuous improvement mindset, and manufacturing/field-quality orientation.

 - Excellent communication skills across Vehicle Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Controls, Supplier Quality, Service Engineering, and Plant Operations.

 - Experience in full life cycle development from concept to prototype to full production.

 - Ability to create testing plan and conduct / coordinate physical tests to prove out design concepts and ensure performance targets are being achieved.

 -Hands-on practical experience in prototype assembly and production assembly with the willingness to assemble your own parts.

 Stability under dynamic constraints

 Scalability across scenarios and vehicle platforms

 Simulation and vehicle logs
